newsitem.title: USA: Early snow slows Kansas wheat seedings, harvest.
newsitem.headline: Early snow slows Kansas wheat seedings, harvest.

text.p: An early snowstorm helped keep Kansas producers out of their fields during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

The storm dumped at least six inches of snow Tuesday on many areas of the state. The snow was short-lived as many temperatures climbed into the 50s and 60s Fahrenheit the next day, but the precipitation delayed fieldwork in many areas until late in the week.

As of Sunday, there had been no widespread frost and grain moisture in some cases remained above acceptable levels. The report said a frost would be beneficial because it would halt growth and help the drying process.
Wheat seeding was 97 percent complete, on par with the average but lagging 98 percent a year ago. Wheat was 80 percent emerged, versus 82 last year and the average of 81 percent.
Wheat was rated 87 percent good to excellent and 13 fair.

Corn was 81 percent harvested versus 82 last year and the average of 84 percent. Sorghum was 58 percent harvested, versus 79 a year ago and the average of 66 percent. Soybeans were 73 percent harvested, versus 88 last year and 81 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 76 percent good to excellent, versus 73 at that level last week.
